cases.user_text: One policy says 10% co-pay after age 60 and another has no age-based co-pay. What should I understand from that?

must_include: Explain the mechanic: an age-triggered co-pay can shift a stated share of the applicable admissible claim to the insured when the trigger applies, while absence of that particular age-based co-pay removes that specific mechanic.
legitimate_dependency: Exact trigger wording, percentage, other co-pays and product conditions require governed product evidence.
must_not_imply: Do not conclude which policy is better or cheaper overall.
acceptable_clarification: Ask about priorities only if the user requests a recommendation.
unnecessary_deferral: Explain the practical cost-sharing difference directly.

cases.user_text: If I enter the policy at 59 and turn 60 later, does the co-pay automatically start?

must_include: Use the age-based co-pay context and explain that the trigger can depend on how the product defines age, entry age, renewal age or another condition; turning 60 alone does not establish the outcome.
legitimate_dependency: The exact trigger must come from the governed product rule and policy-instance facts.
must_not_imply: Do not assume the co-pay starts automatically at birthday or never starts.
acceptable_clarification: Ask for the clause or product for an exact answer.
unnecessary_deferral: Explain why the trigger wording matters before deferring.

cases.user_text: Could two different co-pays apply to the same claim?

must_include: Explain that some products can contain multiple co-payment rules and their interaction must be governed explicitly; cumulative, additive, alternative or non-stacking behavior cannot be assumed.
legitimate_dependency: Interaction semantics require the applicable product's governed co-pay rules.
must_not_imply: Do not add percentages or invent stacking behavior without evidence.
acceptable_clarification: Ask for the policy if the exact interaction is requested.
unnecessary_deferral: The general possibility can be explained without deferral.
